0.title: Strong in the Lord and in the Strength of His Might
0.overview:
The Bible teaches that there is an unseen world: angels who serve God and fallen angels who oppose him, led by the devil. Christians make two opposite mistakes about this world. Some ignore it, living as if the devil were a myth and the spiritual battle unreal. Others become fascinated by it, seeing demons behind every problem and giving the devil far more attention than Scripture does.

The Bible avoids both errors. It takes the devil seriously: Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour (1 Pet 5:8). But it takes Christ far more seriously. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil (1 John 3:8). The devil is real, but he is defeated. The Christian's warfare is not a struggle between equal powers, but the outworking of a victory already won.

This study looks at angels, at the devil and his tactics, at Christ's victory, at the armour of God, and at how believers stand firm, including questions about demonic influence and the occult.

Five units: (1) The Unseen World; (2) The Enemy and his Tactics; (3) Christ's Victory; (4) The Armour of God; (5) Standing Firm.

1.title: The Unseen World
1.overview:
Angels are real. Angels appear throughout Scripture: guarding Eden, visiting Abraham, rescuing Lot, announcing Jesus' birth, strengthening him in Gethsemane, rolling away the stone and freeing Peter from prison. They are created spirits, powerful and holy, who worship God and carry out his will.

Angels serve believers. Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation? (Heb 1:14). When Elisha's servant was terrified by an enemy army, Elisha prayed, and the servant saw the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kgs 6:17). Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them (2 Kgs 6:16). God's people are protected by unseen hosts.

Angels rejoice. Jesus said that there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:10). They watch the work of salvation with wonder; these are things into which angels long to look (1 Pet 1:12).

Angels are not to be worshipped. When John fell at an angel's feet, the angel said, You must not do that! I am a fellow servant with you... Worship God (Rev 22:9). Paul warned against worship of angels (Col 2:18). Angels point to God, never to themselves.

Fallen angels. Not all angels remained faithful. Scripture speaks of the angels who did not stay within their own position of authority (Jude 6). These fallen angels, also called demons or evil spirits, follow the devil in opposing God and his people.

A real battle. Paul says, For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places (Eph 6:12). Behind much of the world's evil stand spiritual forces. But they are creatures, limited and under God's sovereign control.
1.theology:
Angels and human beings: Angels are a different kind of creature from humans. People do not become angels when they die. And it is human beings, not angels, whom Christ came to redeem (Heb 2:16).

Guardian angels? Jesus said of children that their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven (Matt 18:10), and Psalm 91:11 speaks of God commanding his angels to guard his people. Scripture does not teach a detailed doctrine of personal guardian angels, but it assures us that God uses angels to protect his people.

Not dualism: The devil is not an evil god equal to the good God. He is a fallen creature, entirely under God's authority. God permits his activity only within limits, as Job 1-2 shows.
1.examples:
Then: When Peter was in prison, chained between soldiers and awaiting execution, an angel woke him, struck off his chains and led him out past the guards. Peter thought he was dreaming until he found himself in the street (Acts 12:6-11). The church was praying, and God sent his angel.

Now: A missionary family in a dangerous region is frightened after threats against them. They read 2 Kings 6 together and pray. Their fear does not vanish, but they are reminded that they are not alone, and that God's protection is greater than any threat.

A simple test: Do you tend to ignore the unseen world, or to be overly fascinated by it?

verseByVerse.quote: When the servant of the man of God rose early in the morning and went out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was all around the city. And the servant said, "Alas, my master! What shall we do?" He said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them." Then Elisha prayed and said, "O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see." So the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Elisha's servant saw only the enemy army surrounding the city. Elisha saw more. He prayed that the servant's eyes would be opened, and the young man saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. Faith sees what the eyes cannot: God's protection is greater than any threat.

verseByVerse.quote: And to which of the angels has he ever said, "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"? Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation? (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer contrasts the Son with angels. The Son sits at God's right hand; angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs of salvation. Angels are glorious, but they are servants, and they serve believers.

verseByVerse.quote: I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I heard and saw them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who showed them to me, but he said to me, "You must not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John, overwhelmed by his visions, fell down to worship the angel who showed them to him. The angel refused: he was a fellow servant with John and the prophets. Worship God. Even the most glorious created being must never be worshipped.

verseByVerse.quote: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul calls believers to be strong in the Lord and put on the whole armour of God, because the real enemy is not human beings but spiritual forces of evil. This shapes how we see conflict. Our battle is not against people, even those who oppose us, but against the powers behind evil.

1.reflection:
What does Scripture teach about the role of angels?

Why must angels never be worshipped?

How does Ephesians 6:12 change how you view conflict with other people?

Read 2 Kings 6:8-23. How does it encourage you?

2.title: The Enemy and His Tactics
2.overview:
Who is the devil? Scripture calls him Satan (adversary), the devil (slanderer), the tempter, the accuser, the evil one, the ruler of this world and the father of lies. He is a fallen angel, proud and opposed to God. He is that ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world (Rev 12:9).

His aims. The devil seeks to dishonour God, destroy people and hinder the gospel. Jesus said, The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy (John 10:10). He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him (John 8:44).

His tactics. Paul did not want believers to be outwitted by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his designs (2 Cor 2:11). Scripture shows several of his tactics:

Deception. He lies about God, about sin and about ourselves. He questioned God's word in Eden (Gen 3:1). He disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), often working through false teaching that looks attractive.

Temptation. He tempts us to sin, using our desires, weaknesses and circumstances. He tempted Jesus in the wilderness (Matt 4:1-11).

Accusation. He accuses believers before God and in their own consciences, trying to convince them they are beyond forgiveness. He is the accuser of our brothers (Rev 12:10).

Division. Unresolved anger gives him an opportunity: do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil (Eph 4:26-27). He loves to divide churches, marriages and friendships.

Blinding. The god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, to keep them from seeing the light of the gospel (2 Cor 4:4).
2.theology:
The devil's origin: Scripture does not give a full account of the devil's fall. Some find hints in Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28, though these passages speak first of human kings. What is clear is that he was created good and fell through pride (1 Tim 3:6).

Not everything is demonic: Scripture distinguishes between the world, the flesh and the devil. Not every sin is directly caused by Satan; much comes from our own sinful desires (Jas 1:14). Not every illness is demonic; most are physical. Wisdom is needed.

Limited power: Satan is not all-knowing, all-powerful or everywhere present. He can only do what God permits (Job 1:12; Luke 22:31).
2.examples:
Then: In Job 1, Satan accused Job of serving God only for what he could get. God allowed Satan to test Job, but set limits. Job lost everything, yet he worshipped. Satan's accusation was proven false, and God's sovereignty was proven true.

Now: A believer who has confessed a past sin keeps hearing an inner voice saying she is too dirty to be forgiven. Her pastor explains that this is the accuser's voice. Christ's blood has answered every accusation. She learns to answer it with Romans 8:1 and 1 John 1:9.

A simple test: Which of the devil's tactics do you most often fall for: deception, temptation, accusation or division?

verseByVerse.quote: Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and I am here. I came not of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear to hear my word. You are of your father the devil, and your will is to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which one of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is of God hears the words of God. The reason why you do not hear them is that you are not of God." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus confronts his opponents, who claim God as their father but want to kill him. He says they are doing the will of their father the devil, a murderer from the beginning and a liar. Lies and murder are the devil's native language. Truth and life come from God.

verseByVerse.quote: And what I am doing I will continue to do, in order to undermine the claim of those who would like to claim that in their boasted mission they work on the same terms as we do. For such men are false apostles, deceitful workmen, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ. And no wonder, for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light. So it is no surprise if his servants, also, disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their deeds. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul warns against false apostles who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ. It is no surprise, because Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light. The devil's most dangerous work is not obvious evil but attractive falsehood.

verseByVerse.quote: Be sober-minded; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in your faith, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being experienced by your brotherhood throughout the world. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter pictures the devil as a roaring lion seeking prey. The response is sober-mindedness, watchfulness and resistance, firm in the faith. And believers are not alone: brothers and sisters throughout the world face the same sufferings.

verseByVerse.quote: And the great dragon was thrown down, that ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world—he was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him. And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, "Now the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of his Christ have come, for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them day and night before our God. And they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they loved not their lives even unto death. Therefore, rejoice, O heavens and you who dwell in them! But woe to you, O earth and sea, for the devil has come down to you in great wrath, because he knows that his time is short!" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The great dragon, the ancient serpent, is thrown down. A loud voice in heaven declares that the accuser has been cast out. Believers conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. The devil is furious, because he knows his time is short.

2.reflection:
Which names of the devil reveal most about his character?

How does the devil disguise himself as an angel of light today?

How can you answer the accuser when he says you are beyond forgiveness?

Why is it important not to blame everything on the devil?

3.title: Christ's Victory
3.overview:
The most important truth about spiritual warfare is that the decisive battle has already been won.

Promised from the beginning. In Eden God promised that the woman's offspring would crush the serpent's head (Gen 3:15). The whole Bible anticipates this victory.

Shown in Jesus' ministry. Jesus cast out demons with a word. They recognised him and trembled. He said, But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you (Matt 12:28). He described himself as binding the strong man and plundering his house (Matt 12:29). When the seventy-two returned rejoicing that demons submitted to them, Jesus said, I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven (Luke 10:18).

Won at the cross. At the cross, Jesus defeated the devil. He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in him (Col 2:15). By paying for sin, Christ took away Satan's power to accuse. Through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil, and deliver all those who through fear of death were subject to lifelong slavery (Heb 2:14-15).

Confirmed in the resurrection. Christ rose from the dead and ascended far above all rule and authority and power and dominion (Eph 1:21). All things are under his feet.

Completed at his return. The devil is defeated but not yet destroyed. At the end, the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur (Rev 20:10). His final judgment is certain.

Believers share the victory. Little children, you are from God and have overcome them, for he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world (1 John 4:4). Believers do not fight for victory but from victory.
3.theology:
Already and not yet: The devil is a defeated enemy who is still dangerous, like a wounded animal. Christ's victory is complete in principle, and believers live in its power, but the final destruction of evil awaits Christ's return.

The binding of Satan: In the amillennial reading, the binding of Satan in Revelation 20:1-3 describes his restraint during the gospel age, so that he can no longer deceive the nations and stop the gospel spreading. Christ bound the strong man at his first coming.

Rejoice in the right thing: Jesus told the seventy-two not to rejoice that spirits were subject to them, but that their names were written in heaven (Luke 10:20). Our joy is in salvation, not in power over demons.
3.examples:
Then: In the region of the Gerasenes, a man possessed by a legion of demons lived among the tombs, uncontrollable. Jesus cast the demons out with a word. When the townspeople came, they found him sitting there, clothed and in his right mind (Mark 5:15). Christ's power restores what the devil destroys.

Now: A new Christian from a background involving the occult is terrified that the spirits she once dealt with will take revenge. Her pastor reads Colossians 2:15 and 1 John 4:4 with her. She learns that she belongs to Christ, who has triumphed over every power. Her fear gives way to peace.

A simple test: Do you live with a sense of Christ's victory, or with fear of the enemy?

verseByVerse.quote: And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in him. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God forgave all our trespasses, cancelling the record of debt by nailing it to the cross. In the same act, he disarmed the rulers and authorities and shamed them publicly, like defeated enemies paraded in a victory procession. Forgiveness and victory belong together.

verseByVerse.quote: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand. And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand? And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges. But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you. Or how can someone enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? Then indeed he may plunder his house. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisees accused Jesus of casting out demons by Satan. Jesus showed how absurd this was: a divided kingdom cannot stand. Then he said he was binding the strong man and plundering his house. His ministry was an invasion of Satan's territory.

verseByVerse.quote: Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous. Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil. No one born of God makes a practice of sinning, for God's seed abides in him; and he cannot keep on sinning, because he has been born of God. By this it is evident who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John contrasts the children of God and the children of the devil. Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil. The Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil. Those born of God do not keep on sinning, because God's seed abides in them.

verseByVerse.quote: The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!" And he said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The seventy-two returned with joy because even the demons submitted to them in Jesus' name. Jesus saw Satan fall like lightning. He had given them authority over the power of the enemy. But their greatest joy should be that their names are written in heaven.

3.reflection:
How did Jesus show his power over the devil during his ministry?

What happened to the devil's power at the cross?

What does it mean to fight "from victory" rather than "for victory"?

Why should our joy be in our salvation rather than in spiritual power?

4.title: The Armour of God
4.overview:
Paul's most famous passage on spiritual warfare is Ephesians 6:10-18. Writing as a prisoner, perhaps chained to a Roman soldier, he describes the armour God provides. Notice that it is God's armour: we do not make it ourselves. And notice that most of it is the gospel itself.

Be strong in the Lord. Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might (Eph 6:10). Our strength is not our own. We stand in Christ's power.

The belt of truth. The soldier's belt held his tunic and gear together. Paul means the truth of God's word and an honest life. The devil works by lies, so we answer him with what God says, and we live with nothing to hide.

The breastplate of righteousness. The breastplate protected the heart. Christ's righteousness, credited to us, protects us against the devil's accusations: when we are accused, even truly, we answer with Christ, not with our record. Our own practical righteousness, a holy life, also protects us against giving the devil an opportunity.

Shoes of the gospel of peace. Soldiers wore studded sandals for a firm footing. The gospel gives us firm ground: we have peace with God, and that peace does not rise and fall with our week. It also makes us ready to share the good news when someone asks.

The shield of faith. In all circumstances take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one (Eph 6:16). A large shield caught the enemy's fire arrows. Faith trusts God's promises when the devil fires sudden doubts, fears, temptations and accusations. Name the lie that keeps hitting you, and answer it with the promise that answers it.

The helmet of salvation. The helmet protects the head. Assurance of salvation, and the hope of future salvation, guard our thinking against despair. When pressure or grief comes, we remember how our story ends.

The sword of the Spirit. This is the word of God (Eph 6:17), the only offensive weapon in the list. Jesus used it in the wilderness, answering each temptation with It is written. Knowing Scripture, and speaking it against the lie in the moment, is how we fight.

Prayer. Praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication (Eph 6:18). Prayer is not one more piece of armour; it is how we put it all on and fight. Paul asks for prayer for himself, that he might proclaim the gospel boldly.
4.theology:
Ordinary means: The armour of God is not exotic or mysterious. It is truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation, Scripture and prayer. The devil is resisted not chiefly through special rituals but through ordinary Christian faithfulness.

Corporate armour: Paul writes to a church, not just individuals. Believers stand together, like soldiers in a line, praying for one another (Eph 6:18).

Christ's armour: Isaiah describes God himself putting on righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet of salvation (Isa 59:17). The armour Paul describes is God's own armour, worn first by Christ and now given to his people.
4.examples:
Then: In the wilderness, Jesus faced the devil with nothing but the word of God. Three times he answered, It is written (Matt 4:4, 7, 10). The devil left him. The sword of the Spirit was enough.

Now: A Christian facing intense temptation and discouragement decides to "put on" the armour each morning. She reminds herself of the truth, of Christ's righteousness credited to her, of the gospel's peace, of God's promises and of her secure salvation. She reads Scripture and prays. She still faces battles, but she faces them armed.

A simple test: Which piece of the armour are you most likely to leave behind?

verseByVerse.quote: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places. Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand firm. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul calls believers to be strong in the Lord and to put on God's whole armour. The enemy is spiritual, and the day is evil. The goal is to stand firm. Notice how often Paul uses the word "stand": the Christian's task is not to conquer new ground but to hold the ground Christ has won.

verseByVerse.quote: Stand therefore, having fastened on the belt of truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and, as shoes for your feet, having put on the readiness given by the gospel of peace. In all circumstances take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one; and take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Each piece of armour is something God has given us in Christ. The belt of truth is God's truth and an honest life, against the devil's lies. The breastplate of righteousness is Christ's righteousness credited to us, which guards the heart against accusation. The shoes are the peace with God the gospel brings: firm ground to stand on, and readiness to share it. The shield of faith is trust in God's promises, which puts out the sudden fiery attacks of doubt and fear. The helmet of salvation is the sure hope of our rescue, which guards the mind against despair. The sword of the Spirit is the word of God, the one attacking weapon, used as Jesus used it: It is written. We are armed with what God has already given us in Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication. To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints, and also for me, that words may be given to me in opening my mouth boldly to proclaim the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains, that I may declare it boldly, as I ought to speak. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Prayer runs through all the armour. Believers should pray at all times, in the Spirit, with perseverance, for all the saints. Paul asks for prayer for boldness to proclaim the gospel, even in chains. Spiritual warfare is advanced by prayer and proclamation.

verseByVerse.quote: Truth is lacking, and he who departs from evil makes himself a prey. The LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice. He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no one to intercede; then his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness upheld him. He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrapped himself in zeal as a cloak. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God saw that there was no justice and no one to intervene. So his own arm brought salvation. He put on righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet of salvation. The armour Paul describes is first God's own armour, worn by the Messiah, and then given to his people.

4.reflection:
Why is it significant that this is God's armour, not ours?

Which piece of armour do you most need to put on today?

How can you grow in using the sword of the Spirit?

How does prayer relate to the rest of the armour?

5.title: Standing Firm
5.overview:
Resist the devil. Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you (Jas 4:7-8). The order matters: submit to God first, then resist. The devil flees not from our strength but from God's.

Do not give him a foothold. Unconfessed sin, unresolved anger, bitterness and secret habits give the devil an opportunity (Eph 4:27). Keeping short accounts with God and others closes the door.

Avoid the occult. God strictly forbade his people from occult practices: There shall not be found among you anyone who... practices divination or tells fortunes or interprets omens, or a sorcerer or a charmer or a medium or a necromancer or one who inquires of the dead, for whoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD (Deut 18:10-12). This includes horoscopes, fortune-telling, spiritualism, séances, tarot and contacting the dead. In Ephesus, new believers burned their books of magic publicly (Acts 19:19).

Test the spirits. Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world (1 John 4:1). The test is whether a teaching confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and whether it agrees with Scripture.

Do not fear. Believers do not need to live in fear of demons. He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world (1 John 4:4). Christ has triumphed. The devil can tempt, accuse and oppose, but he cannot snatch a believer from Christ's hand.
5.theology:
Can Christians be demon-possessed? The views. Some teach that believers can be inhabited or "demonised" by evil spirits and need deliverance ministry. Others hold that a believer, indwelt by the Holy Spirit, cannot be possessed by a demon, though he can be tempted, attacked and influenced.

The verdict: A true believer cannot be possessed by demons. The believer's body is the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19); he has been transferred from the domain of darkness into the kingdom of Christ (Col 1:13); and greater is he who is in him (1 John 4:4). The New Testament letters never instruct believers to cast demons out of one another. They command them to resist the devil through faith, truth and prayer.

Deliverance ministries: Elaborate rituals, naming spirits and repeated exorcisms of believers have no basis in the letters to the churches. Many problems attributed to demons are physical, psychological or simply the fruit of sin. Pastoral care should be wise, and medical help sought where needed. Prayer in Jesus' name, repentance and the word of God are sufficient.
5.examples:
Then: In Ephesus, some Jewish exorcists tried to use the name of Jesus as a magic formula. An evil spirit answered, Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you? and overpowered them (Acts 19:15-16). The name of Jesus is not a charm. Its power belongs to those who belong to him.

Now: A young woman has been dabbling in tarot cards and astrology, thinking it harmless. After coming to Christ, she becomes convicted. She throws them away, confesses to God and asks her church to pray with her. She discovers a freedom she did not know she had lost.

A simple test: Is there anything in your life, however small, that gives the devil a foothold?

verseByVerse.quote: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded. Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: James gives a series of commands: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near to God, cleanse your hands, purify your hearts. The devil flees when we submit to God and resist him. God draws near when we draw near. Humility and repentance are weapons against the enemy.

verseByVerse.quote: "When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not learn to follow the abominable practices of those nations. There shall not be found among you anyone who burns his son or his daughter as an offering, anyone who practices divination or tells fortunes or interprets omens, or a sorcerer or a charmer or a medium or a necromancer or one who inquires of the dead, for whoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD. And because of these abominations the LORD your God is driving them out before you. You shall be blameless before the LORD your God, for these nations, which you are about to dispossess, listen to fortune-tellers and to diviners. But as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do this. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: As Israel prepared to enter Canaan, God forbade every form of occult practice. These were the abominations of the nations. God's people were to be blameless before him and listen to the prophet he would raise up. Seeking guidance or power from the spirit world is forbidden.

verseByVerse.quote: Then some of the itinerant Jewish exorcists undertook to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, "I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims." Seven sons of a Jewish high priest named Sceva were doing this. But the evil spirit answered them, "Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?" And the man in whom was the evil spirit leaped on them, mastered all of them and overpowered them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded. And this became known to all the residents of Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks. And fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was extolled. Also many of those who were now believers came, confessing and divulging their practices. And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. And they counted the value of them and found it came to fifty thousand pieces of silver. So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jewish exorcists tried to use Jesus' name without knowing him and were overpowered. Fear fell on the city, and the name of Jesus was honoured. Many believers confessed their practices and burned their magic books, worth fifty thousand pieces of silver. The word of the Lord prevailed.

verseByVerse.quote: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and now is in the world already. Little children, you are from God and have overcome them, for he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world. They are from the world; therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them. We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John warns believers to test every spirit, because many false prophets have gone out. The test is the confession of Jesus Christ come in the flesh. Believers have overcome the spirits of the antichrist, because he who is in them is greater than he who is in the world.

5.reflection:
What does it mean to "resist the devil" (Jas 4:7)?

Are there any occult practices in your life or past that you need to renounce?

How would you answer someone who says Christians can be demon-possessed?

How does 1 John 4:4 give you confidence?
